text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says the Anti-Corruption Agency has a free hand to investigate the allegations of corruption and property ownership against the chief minister of Selangor state.
-- Malaysia offers Pakistan help to offset trade imbalances between the two countries.
-- Malaysian state railway firm KTM Bhd gives remaining illegal tenants on its land in Singapore another 48 hours to move out.
-- Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek says more than half of the construction sites in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor state are unsafe for workers.
-- A shark thought to have been extinct was caught in a river in Sabah state.
